intended_object: A certificate (`IsLimit` data) that the explicitly built cone `GrpCat.limitCone F` is a limit cone of a diagram `F : J ⥤ GrpCat`. The cone is the group of compatible families (the sections) with pointwise operations. This comes from the docstring and the name.
explanation: This is not a mathematical object. It is the proof, packaged as `IsLimit` data, that the chosen cone in the group category has the universal property of a limit. Mathematically it is the theorem "the group of compatible families is the limit of the diagram". The construction comes from `liftedLimitIsLimit`: the forgetful functor to types creates the limit. The hypothesis `Small.{u}` on the sections is exactly the condition under which the limit cone exists in `GrpCat.{u}`, so it does not narrow anything. The docstring itself says users should normally use `limit.cone F`, which marks this as library infrastructure, not a definition of a new notion. It is correct as stated.
